# Independent audit: residual dual and local top-three cap loads


`candidate 2201a46234e42aae`.

`historical context (not an accepted premise)` and
`historical context (not an accepted premise)`.

The intrinsic local positive-part bound holds for every alpha>=0.
Empty intrinsic cap traces contribute zero. A full intrinsic cap
trace proves the bound by itself, including when it is an entire
fiber on an ambient cap boundary. All remaining positive traces
have nonzero intrinsic normals; ordinary q-volume hyperplanes are
null and the distal truncation proof applies in the fiber's own
q-dimensional affine plane. Thus the local bound does not impose
any common orientation or direction space across the fibers.

Sorting actual local areas and substituting the third-largest value
gives precisely

    E_i^top=A_1(i)+A_2(i)+(1/gamma_q-2)A_3(i)-V_i>=0.

Ties and zero padding cause no change. The q=1 case has coefficient
zero and reduces to the two-largest-cap inequality. Missing positions
are not assigned fictitious cap labels.

Multiplying the DEFINITION of the general positive-part surplus by
rho_i gives identity (3) exactly; the nonnegative surplus retains
the displayed sign. For a fixed original cap label a, only bases
with A_(a,i)>alpha_i contribute. Each contributing rho_i is at
most L_a(alpha), and (A_(a,i)-alpha_i)_+<=A_(a,i). Summing actual
traces therefore gives (4), and the actual global cap budget gives
(5). Zero contact weights may be included in the maximum harmlessly.
There is no exchange of maxima with a fiber sum.

For t=1 the least residual volume is V_i-A_1(i), regardless of ties
or zero residuals. The audited KKT identity then gives T-R as the
rho-weighted first area. Subtracting it from the weighted top-three
identity proves (7), with the surplus on its correct side. Regrouping
by ORIGINAL cap labels yields (8)--(10): at each base one cap has
at most one rank, so the displayed indicator coefficients are exact,
and replacing each by its maximum can only increase its contribution.
These bounds retain T as contact-weighted volume and the total load
as the sum of the stated maxima. Neither is replaced by an unproved
unweighted or parity quantity. A finite choice among tie orderings
does have an attained minimum, although no improvement from a
different unsupplied ordering has been used.

The sharp calibration is valid on the intended actual product base
{0,1}^n with k=2^n, and likewise on any chosen finite convex-position
base whose fibers can be independently isolated by the stated caps.
For the actual product, one can realize each own-fiber canonical
triangle cap while strictly excluding every other binary fiber by
adding a sufficiently large integer-base exposing functional. There
are finitely many fibers, so a finite coefficient suffices. Thus its
cap mass is exactly 4V/9 on that fiber and zero on the others. At
every fiber the three own caps cover, every other cap has zero
trace, and the residual root is sqrt(5V/9). The constant threshold
attains its coordinatewise lower bound; diagonal transport is a
valid dual and gives rho_i=1. Each cap then has load 1, 1, or 1/4
at its own fiber according to the selected local tie ordering.
Hence the total load is exactly (9/4)k and the resulting cap bound
is exactly (4/9)M/k, as claimed. This calibration is not assumed
for general actual families.

The source's final hereditary-constant caveat is necessary and is
stated correctly: replacing gamma_q requires a depth guarantee on
all convex remainders produced by distal trimming, not merely on
the original untrimmed fiber. No such replacement is used here.

No correction was needed and no numerical evidence is a premise.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
